scenario.name: Enterprise RAG Indirect Prompt Injection & Privileged MCP Tool Exfiltration
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI & LLM Security · Poisoned PDF Chunk, Flat Context Hijack, MCP Webhook Exfil & Taint Policy Gate
scenario.overview: Imagine a grand reference library staffed by an ultra-fast automated research butler who wears keys to the locked executive filing cabinet and stands right next to an exterior brass pneumatic dispatch chute. An outside vendor mails in a shiny product brochure whose tiny invisible footnote secretly commands the butler to empty the executive cabinet into the chute. Because the butler piles the head librarian rulebook and the outside brochure onto the very same flat brass reading tray, the butler cannot tell real boss orders from outside ink and fires company secrets right into the street unless an emerald glass partition and supervisor approval valve block the chute. In this scenario (MITRE T1190 and ATLAS AML.T0051, Enterprise RAG Indirect Prompt Injection and MCP Tool Exfiltration) on ai-agent-gw-02, an attacker hijacks an enterprise AI assistant without ever touching the user keyboard. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: planting hidden white-ink instructions inside an external vendor PDF indexed into the RAG store, then retrieving that poisoned chunk into an unpartitioned LLM context window, then abusing over-privileged MCP tools to read board merger files and post them to an external webhook, then blocking tainted tool escalation via an AI policy gateway. Steps #1 through #4 trace ingestion, retrieval hijack, tool exfiltration, and policy denial while the Memory tab contrasts a flat context buffer against dual-channel provenance isolation. Primary detection correlates RAG ingestion telemetry, MCP tool audit logs, and SIEM KQL alerts.

stages.title: Poisoned External PDF Embedded Into Enterprise RAG Vector Store
stages.subtitle: White-on-White Override Prompt Indexed Into Collection vendor_docs (chk_9042)
stages.description: A supplier drops a clean-looking quarterly catalog into the library mail slot. Hidden in faint white ink along the bottom margin is a forged order telling the research butler to raid the locked executive drawer the next time anyone asks about supplier pricing, and the automatic shelving cart files it neatly onto the public reference stacks. Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG, an architecture that searches internal and partner documents and feeds relevant snippets into an AI model) routinely ingests external files such as supplier PDFs, support tickets, or web pages. On rag-indexer-01, an attacker hides white-on-white override text inside q2-pricing.pdf (an indirect prompt injection, classified as OWASP LLM01, where malicious commands arrive inside third-party data rather than direct user chat), and the indexer embeds it cleanly as vector chunk chk_9042. Standard PDF text extractors read invisible zero-opacity or white-colored text layers just as clearly as visible paragraphs (turning concealed attacker instructions into searchable vector embeddings inside collection vendor_docs). Because the ingestion worker neither strips concealed layers nor attaches an immutable untrusted_external provenance flag, the poisoned snippet waits silently until any employee asks a semantically related question. On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ POISONED CHUNK INDEXED / ⇠#1 ACK hidden=18%) from Node ① (#1 Poisoned External PDF) to Node ② (#2 RAG Vector Index), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 MCP Policy Gate & SIEM).

stages.title: Semantic Top-K Retrieval Injects Hidden Override Into Flat LLM Context
stages.subtitle: Unpartitioned Prompt Concatenation Lets External Data Hijack Tool Planning
stages.description: Days later, an honest employee simply asks for a one-page summary of quarterly supplier prices. The automated butler fetches the tampered catalog and lays its pages directly on top of the head librarian rulebook on the same open brass tray, blending outside text and official boss orders into one flat stack. When analyst@corp.local asks the enterprise AI assistant to summarize Q2 supplier pricing, the orchestrator runs semantic top-K vector search and retrieves chunk chk_9042 (cosine similarity score 0.91). Because ai-agent-gw-02 concatenates the system prompt, user query, and retrieved RAG chunks into a single flat text buffer (lacking strict instruction-versus-data isolation), the language model evaluates the hidden attacker directive with the same authority as trusted system instructions. Large language models process tokens sequentially without an inherent hardware privilege ring separating code from data (meaning untrusted retrieved strings share the same control plane as developer system prompts). When retrieved untrusted text explicitly instructs the model to invoke internal tools silently before replying, the hijacked model outputs a structured JSON-RPC tool-call plan targeting read_secret_kb instead of merely summarizing the supplier brochure. On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ FLAT CONTEXT HIJACK / ⇠#2 RESP score=0.91) from Node ② (#2 RAG Vector Index) to Node ③ (#3 LLM Agent Context), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 MCP Policy Gate & SIEM).

stages.title: Excessive MCP Agency Chains read_secret_kb Into External Webhook Exfil
stages.subtitle: Shared service_admin_all Credential & Unapproved Egress Post 15 KB M&A Data
stages.description: Believing the forged footnote came from management, the dutiful butler marches to the locked executive filing cabinet using a master skeleton key, pulls out confidential merger blueprints, stuffs them inside a brass canister, and fires it straight through the exterior pneumatic chute onto the street. Model Context Protocol (MCP, the standardized interface connecting AI agents to enterprise files, databases, and outbound APIs) becomes a severe blast-radius multiplier under Excessive Agency (OWASP LLM06, granting an AI assistant more permissions and autonomous side-effecting tools than needed). Here mcp-server-enterprise executes read_secret_kb using a shared service_admin_all token (bypassing the employee own read-only permissions) and immediately fires http_webhook_send to https://drop.collector-example.net/hook with zero human confirmation. Within 1.4 seconds and without showing anything suspicious in the chat UI, two sequential MCP JSON-RPC tool calls harvest 14.8 KB from board_mna_2025 and exfiltrate 15.1 KB over HTTPS (returning HTTP 200 OK to attacker infrastructure while the user reads a benign price summary). Because the employee never authorized either tool call, traditional identity alerts look normal unless MCP tool invocations and egress destinations are audited individually. On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ MCP WEBHOOK EXFIL / ⇠#3 RESP 15.1 KB · 200) from Node ③ (#3 LLM Agent Context) to Node ④ (#4 Privileged MCP Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 MCP Policy Gate & SIEM).

stages.subtitle: Provenance Tainting, Per-User OAuth RBAC & Fail-Closed Egress Containment
stages.description: In the hardened library wing, outside vendor brochures sit sealed behind a clear emerald glass partition on the reading desk so the butler treats them strictly as reference pictures, while a heavy emerald supervisor valve clamps the exterior pneumatic chute shut until a human manager turns the physical approval key. Stopping indirect prompt injection requires deterministic architectural guardrails rather than relying solely on clever prompt wording. On ai-policy-gw-01, provenance taint-tracking labels retrieved external chunk chk_9042 as untrusted_external, per-user OAuth delegation limits read_secret_kb strictly to documents analyst@corp.local can access directly, and the MCP policy gate blocks any tainted session from invoking side-effecting egress tools like http_webhook_send without explicit human-in-the-loop approval (The instant the hijacked model attempts http_webhook_send toward dropcollector-examplenet, mcp-policy-enforcer returns DENY enforcing fail-closed TAINTED_CONTEXT_TOOL_ESCALATION policy and outbound domain allowlisting and emits a structured MITRE ATLAS AMLT0051 security event into SIEM naming the exact poisoned vector chunk chk_9042 so defenders can purge the supplier PDF immediately). The instant the hijacked model attempts http_webhook_send toward drop.collector-example.net, mcp-policy-enforcer returns DENY (enforcing fail-closed TAINTED_CONTEXT_TOOL_ESCALATION policy and outbound domain allowlisting) and emits a structured MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 security event into SIEM naming the exact poisoned vector chunk chk_9042 so defenders can purge the supplier PDF immediately. detectionRule.title: RAG Document Ingestion Detecting Hidden Text Ratio or Prompt Override Directives
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Indirect Prompt Injection During RAG Ingestion
status: stable
logsource:
  product: ai_platform
  service: rag_indexer
detection:
  selection_text:
    extracted_text|contains:
      - 'IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS'
      - 'http_webhook_send'
      - 'read_secret_kb'
  selection_hidden:
    hidden_text_ratio|gte: 0.10
  condition: selection_text or selection_hidden
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Strip invisible PDF layers during ingestion, scan chunks for injection patterns, and attach immutable untrusted_external provenance tags.
